messages:
maya: Heads up — cost spike in eu-west-1 spot pool. A100 spot price jumped ~1.8x and available capacity is H100/L4 heavy. Thinking through mixing GPU types in a single spot pool vs separate lanes. Any quick wins?
aditya: I saw the same. Evictions up ~3x last 90m. Some jobs got moved to smaller SKUs mid-run which caused failures.
liam: My 2c: mixing too many families in one binpack group causes fragmentation. Preferring iso-arch packing reduces cross-arch migrations and KV cache thrash.
sophia: Could do prioritized fallback lanes: primary lane = A100/H100 (latency sensitive), fallback lane = L4 (batch). But model perf differences matter.
jorge: Do we have perf/cost delta numbers? Especially for p95 latency and cost per token across families.
aditya: Quick numbers from the recent bench run:
```
A100: p95=45ms cost=0.12 $/k-token
H100: p95=48ms cost=0.10 $/k-token
L4:  p95=90ms cost=0.045 $/k-token
```
(adjusted for batch=1) — L4 is cheap but latency ~2x.
sophia: That fits expectations. Recommendation: route inference traffic by SLO. Low-latency requests only to A100/H100 pool; background/cached or best-effort to L4.
maya: Also worried about multi-GPU models that need >80GB. L4s won't fit those. We should binpack by memory footprint and GPU family.
liam: Agreed. Multi-instance-type fleets are good but keep family-aware subpools. e.g., pool-a100, pool-h100, pool-l4. Then scheduler can chase price within a family first.
jorge: Fragmentation problem: many small slots of different shapes. Suggest size-buckets: tiny (<30GB), mid (30-80GB), large (>80GB) and pack accordingly.
aditya: Small placement policy sketch: 
```
placement_policy:
  - name: latency
    families: [a100,h100]
    mem_buckets: ["mid","large"]
  - name: batch
    families: [l4]
    mem_buckets: ["tiny","mid"]
```
(scheduler chooses cheapest in family & bucket, fallback to next family only if strict capacity shortfall)
sophia: Also watch network/PCIe differences. H100 NVLink topology can matter for multi-GPU throughput — treating H100 as separate class improves multi-GPU perf predictability.
maya: Plan: I will spin up a canary experiment — 20% of traffic in eu-west-1 diverted to a hetero-fallback policy that prefers iso-arch packing and uses L4 for batch jobs. Will track evictions, latency, cost/token, and failure rate.
autoscaler-bot: Created experiment 'hetero-fallback-canary-1932104567' in eu-west-1 — rollout: 20% :rocket:
sophia: Good. Add a regression alert for p99 latency and a token-rate drop probe so we don't silently regress throughput.
liam: Also add a metric for KG (KV cache) miss rate; migrations spike that.
maya: Will open a short doc with recommendations and the experiment dashboard links. TL;DR: keep family lanes, iso-arch packing for low-latency, L4 lane for batch, size-buckets for binpack.
aditya: :thumbsup:
